question: Asked whether to buy a $14.99 film, most said yes. What changed when not buying was phrased as keeping $14.99 for other things?
answer: Fewer people bought it. In Frederick and colleagues' study, buying fell from about 75% to about 55% once the alternative was spelled out as keeping the money for other purchases. Everyone knew the money could go elsewhere; they simply did not think of it until reminded. Every yes quietly spends something on a no.
move: Name what a yes takes away before you give it.
ask: What will my next yes quietly take from my evenings, my money or my energy?
trap: Stating such an obvious alternative seems bound to change nothing.
source: Frederick and colleagues, J. Consumer Research, 2009
reference: Frederick, Novemsky, Wang, Dhar and Nowlis, Opportunity Cost Neglect, Journal of Consumer Research, 2009
